items.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016
items.q: Charlie Persip, you know? I had cats teaching me that played with Bird.

ctx.x: Right. Charlie Persip, you know? I had cats teaching me that played with Bird. You know what I mean? So that’s a different thing. Because they were around all those individual cats and they understand the thing. They’re not failed musicians or anything, they’re in schools because they want to teach us, give us what they know. Not because that’s all they got. And so before music became a music business per se, it was really cool to be yourself and have your own voice. And that’s what it was about. Who’s different?…

it’s literally like three artists you’ve got to fit in that mold. If you’re a black singer and you are a male you’ve got to fit somewhere in the Chris Brown mold. You know? If you’re female you’ve got to fit in the Beyoncé mold. You know I went to high school with Beyoncé. So that’s another individual that I know — I knew her for a long time. You know. But those are certain molds that people say okay, now we need you to be like that because that makes money, versus people taking the time. You know they used to…
